page: Amazon Web Services m8g.medium is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the AWS Graviton4 generation architecture. The instance provides 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) based on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor family running at 2.8 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of memory. It features 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache, with hardware acceleration for AES cryptographic operations. It does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, relying on external network storage solutions, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate competent single-core processing capabilities alongside standard single-thread throughput limitations. In single-core evaluations, the server achieves an average standing with a Geekbench single-core score of 1731.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1694.09, accompanied by strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.0 GB/sec. However, because the instance is provisioned with only a single core and single thread, overall multi-core and throughput-focused metrics place in the lowest percentiles. Memory bandwidth achieves 30.06 GB/sec read and 11.5 GB/sec write on 256MB blocks, with static web serving measured at 2.43 GB/sec and Redis SET operations yielding 2.34 million operations per second.

The m8g.medium instance delivers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio within an entry-level footprint, providing dedicated non-burstable core execution. Given its low total compute capacity and absence of bundled local disks, the configuration is best suited for lightweight web serving, small background workers, microservices, edge orchestration nodes, and basic development or testing environments that require 64-bit ARM architecture without heavy concurrent parallelism.
